name: ProtoDUNE-SP demonstrates full-scale single-phase LArTPC performance
notes: date_kind is publication: JINST 15 (2020) P12004; the arXiv preprint (2007.06722) was posted in July 2020.
This is a construction/technology milestone, not a physics discovery, evidence claim or measurement; DUNE has not yet published an oscillation-physics result (task scope note).

significance.note: A technology milestone, not a physics measurement; no single headline number is quoted.

summary.plain: DUNE built and tested a full-size slice of its liquid-argon detector technology at CERN with a beam of particles, to prove the design works before building the real thing underground.
summary.technical: ProtoDUNE-SP (NP04), a 770 t single-phase LArTPC built at the CERN Neutrino Platform, was exposed to a charged-particle beam of 0.3-7 GeV/c; the paper reports the detector's first operational performance (drift, purity, calorimetric response) validating the technology for the DUNE far-detector modules.

title: First results on ProtoDUNE-SP liquid argon time projection chamber performance from a beam test at the CERN Neutrino Platform
why_it_matters: ProtoDUNE-SP proved that DUNE's single-phase liquid-argon TPC technology works at close to full detector-module scale before the collaboration committed to building the far-detector modules underground at SURF.
